finances.howItWorksBody: Each player's share is calculated based on the number of nights they attend relative to the total number of person-nights for the selected event. Players with more nights contribute more. RSVP "in" on the event and confirm your arrival/departure dates to appear in this calculation. From the first day of the LAN, dates are locked: only the treasurer or an admin can change them.

settings.currencySectionDesc: Choose the currency symbol used across the app — expenses, event budgets and the pro-rata split.
settings.currencyDesc: Applies everywhere amounts are shown. Existing amounts are not converted — only the symbol changes.
settings.featuresSectionDesc: Turn optional features on or off for the whole crew.
settings.treasuryToggleDesc: Expense tracking and the pro-rata cost split. Turn off if you're hosting and covering all costs yourself — this hides the Treasury page, its nav link, the dashboard budget stat and per-event expenses. No data is deleted; re-enabling brings it all back.
settings.sponsorsToggleDesc: Show sponsor banners for brand-funded events. Manage each event's sponsors on its page; banners then appear on the event, tournaments and player profile pages.
settings.prizesToggleDesc: Showcase prizes (photo + description) per event. Enabling Prizes takes the Treasury's place — Treasury is hidden while this is on, since crews giving prizes usually don't split expenses.
settings.planningToggleDesc: Let the crew propose games and vote on which hours to play them, bounded by each player's RSVP window. Adds a Planning page and nav link. Off by default.
settings.planningProposeToggleDesc: When on, any member can add a game to the schedule. When off, only admins propose — members still vote. This is the global default; each event can override it.
settings.planningVoteToggleDesc: When on, members approval-vote on time slots (the democratic heatmap). When off, the organizer decides. This is the global default; each event can override it.
settings.announcementsSectionDesc: Post a message to the whole crew — it shows as a dismissible banner across the app. Great for "Pizza's here" or "Finals in 5". Optionally fan it out to your Discord webhook.
settings.twitchDesc: Enter your Twitch Developer app credentials to enable live status badges on the Streams page. Create an app at
settings.twitchClientIdDesc: From dev.twitch.tv — used to fetch live stream metadata.
settings.twitchClientSecretDesc: Keep this secret. Used with Client ID to get an app access token.
settings.discordSsoDesc: Let players sign in and register with their Discord account. Create an application and copy its OAuth2 credentials from
settings.discordOauthEnabledDesc: Shows a 'Continue with Discord' button on the login and registration pages.
settings.discordOauthClientIdDesc: The application's OAuth2 Client ID from the Discord developer portal.
settings.discordOauthClientSecretDesc: Keep this secret. Used to exchange the login code for the player's Discord profile.
settings.discordSsoRedirectHint: Add this exact redirect URI to your Discord app (OAuth2 → Redirects):
settings.steamLinkDesc: Let players link their Steam account from their profile, to import their owned games into their library. Get a free Web API key at
settings.steamLinkEnabledDesc: Shows a 'Link Steam' button on the profile page. Steam login itself needs no credentials — the API key below is only used to fetch a linked player's display name and owned games.
settings.steamWebApiKeyDesc: Free key from steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey. Used to fetch a linked player's profile and owned-games list, never for the sign-in step itself.
settings.steamLinkRedirectHint: Steam needs no redirect URI configured on their side, but this app's own callback is:
settings.discordDesc: Set your crew's Discord invite link, and optionally a webhook URL so event reminders and new-event announcements post straight into a channel (e.g. "LAN-PARTY") instead of email.
settings.discordInviteDesc: e.g. https://discord.gg/your-invite-code — shown as an icon in the Navbar for every logged-in player.
settings.discordWebhookDesc: Channel Settings → Integrations → Webhooks in Discord. Leave blank to disable — no other feature depends on it.
settings.appTimezoneDesc: IANA format, e.g. Europe/Paris — reminders are sent at 10am in this timezone. Changes take effect after a backend restart.
settings.reminderDaysDesc: How many days before an event's start date to post a reminder. Default: 3.
settings.discordTemplatesIntro: Customize the wording of Discord messages (Markdown supported: **bold**, etc.). Available placeholders: {{event_title}}, {{start_date}}, {{end_date}}, {{location}}, {{app_base_url}}.
settings.discordReminderDesc: Posted once per event, N days before it starts, if at least one attendee is RSVP'd in.
settings.discordAnnouncementDesc: Posted once when an admin creates a new event.
settings.discordTestDesc: Post a sample message to your Discord channel to confirm the webhook and templates render correctly. Uses fake event details.
settings.discordTestNoWebhook: Set a Discord webhook URL above to enable test messages.
settings.emailDesc: Configure an SMTP account so users can reset a forgotten password themselves. Leave the host blank to disable — admins can still reset a user's password manually from their profile.
settings.smtpHostDesc: e.g. smtp.gmail.com — leave blank to disable email sending.
settings.smtpPasswordDesc: For Gmail/Outlook, use an app password, not your account password.
settings.smtpFromDesc: The address recipients will see as the sender.
settings.smtpTlsDesc: Type "true" or "false". Leave as true unless your provider says otherwise.
settings.appBaseUrlDesc: Public URL of this instance, e.g. https://lan.example.com — used to build the password-reset link.
settings.backupDesc: Download a compressed archive of the database and all uploaded media files.
settings.restoreDesc: Upload a .tar.gz backup to replace the current database and uploads. This overwrites ALL current data — the server will restart automatically and you may need to log in again.
settings.restoreConfirm: This will overwrite ALL current data (database and uploads) with the contents of this backup. A safety copy of the current database is kept as lanparty.db.pre-restore.bak. Continue?
settings.restoreDone: Restore complete — the server is restarting, reloading shortly...
settings.restoreError: Restore failed — the backup may be invalid. No data was changed.
settings.storageSectionDesc: How much disk space is left on the volume behind your media uploads — the one thing in this app that can grow without an obvious ceiling.
settings.storageLowWarning: Running low on disk space — uploads may start failing soon.
settings.deploymentDescPrefix: Pull from Docker Hub and run with a single
settings.kioskSectionDesc: A full-screen, unattended display for a projector or TV — rotating matches, standings, arrivals, the schedule and a photo wall, with champion celebrations and announcement flashes. Enable it, then open the link on the big-screen machine.
settings.kioskToggleDesc: Exposes a token-authorized, read-only /kiosk display. Off by default.
settings.kioskLiveDropDesc: A photo or video posted while the big screen runs takes over the display with a full-screen reveal — at most one every 45 s, several posts at once are grouped. On by default.
settings.kioskNoToken: Generate a kiosk link to open the big-screen display on your projector.
settings.kioskTokenHint: Anyone with this link can view the big-screen display (no login, read-only, no emails or finances). Rotate or revoke it to invalidate a shared link.
settings.gearToggleDesc: Per-event 'who's bringing what' — members pledge kit, admins post requests, and your usual gear carries over. Off by default.
settings.recapToggleDesc: An auto-generated highlight page for a finished event — champion, MVP, nights, photos and badges — with an optional public share link that never includes money. Off by default.
settings.setupToggleDesc: Let members show off their gaming PC on their profile — parts, custom fields and up to 5 photos — with an optional public link they mint and revoke themselves. Off by default.
settings.streamsToggleDesc: Twitch channel and clip curation, with a live badge and optional chat. Turn off if your crew has no streamer — this hides the Live page and its nav link. On by default.
settings.checklistToggleDesc: A private per-event packing checklist for every member — 9 pre-filled items plus up to 10 custom fields, with a one-tap 'copy my usual list' for the next event. Only the member who fills it in can ever see it. Off by default.
settings.merchSizeToggleDesc: Let members set a t-shirt/merch size on their profile. Turn off if you're not doing event merch — this hides the Merch size step on Profile and stops it gating profile completeness. On by default.
settings.cravingChatToggleDesc: A lightweight per-event hype chat on the Hub, open to confirmed attendees from 30 days before an event through 15 days after. Turn off if your crew doesn't need another chat channel. On by default.
settings.removedUsersSectionDesc: Accounts an admin has permanently deleted — they no longer appear anywhere in the app (including the HUB roster), this is just a record of who's gone and when.
settings.minigamesToggleDesc: Embedded arcade games with a per-player leaderboard, to keep the crew around between LANs. Only solo runs are ranked.
settings.gamesToggleDesc: Lets members list the games they own (with a max player count) and a wishlist on their profile, and browse the crew by shared games — "what do we play tonight?". Off by default.
settings.groceriesToggleDesc: A per-event food/drink shopping list — any attendee can add an item, assign who's buying it, and tick it off once bought. No price field; cost splitting stays in Treasury. Off by default.
settings.wifiSectionDesc: The spare network for phones and laptops — PCs stay wired. Shown on the big screen and, for its attendees, on the current event's page.
settings.wifiSsidDesc: Leave empty to hide the WiFi everywhere.
settings.wifiPasswordDesc: Visible to admins, to members attending the current event, and on the big screen. Use a dedicated guest network.
settings.wifiSecurityDesc: WPA covers WPA, WPA2 and WPA3.
settings.wifiHiddenDesc: Turn on if the network doesn't broadcast its name.
settings.wifiEmptyHint: No network name set — the WiFi is hidden everywhere.
settings.wifiPreviewDesc: Scan it with your phone before the LAN: it should offer to join the network. The big screen shows this code, the network name and the password.
settings.wifiNoBaseUrlWarning: The app URL (Email section) is empty: the big screen will use its own address for the "Open LPM" code. Make sure phones on this WiFi can reach it.
settings.trophiesToggleDesc: Crew-defined trophies awarded at each LAN — by the attendees' vote or by an admin — and kept for good on the winners' profiles, the recap and the big screen.
settings.lolStatsToggleDesc: Records every League of Legends game the members finish, sent by their desktop app (customs, ARAM, ranked, tournament matches), and shows K/D/A, damage and records per player in Games > League of Legends tracker, overall or per LAN. Each member can choose, in their app, to only send LAN games. Players are matched by the Riot ID on their profile. Off by default.
settings.xpToggleDesc: Members earn XP from what they already do on LPM (tournament wins by stage, titles, revealed trophies, photos in Media, the Craving Chat, a profile picture) and level up with an LPM token. Shown on profiles and as a crew ranking on the Hub. Computed from existing data, so past LANs count too. Off by default.
settings.trophiesSectionDesc: Your crew's own trophies, in your own words. Define them here once; put them in play and award them from each event's page. A trophy that has been won is archived, never deleted.

lol.setupIntro: The desktop app sends every League of Legends game you finish on its own — customs, ARAM, ranked or tournament matches. Those played during a LAN you're attending also count for that LAN. For yours to count, two things to set up:
lol.desktopHint: Install the desktop app (Windows) and keep it open while you play: it reads the League client's end-of-game screen and sends it here. Nothing else on your PC is touched. In its settings (⚙), you can keep your games outside a LAN to yourself.
